questions.question: What is the main economic purpose of insurance?
choices: To guarantee a profit from every purchase
To replace a household's regular wages permanently
To help manage the financial consequences of covered risks
To eliminate the possibility of accidents

questions.question: What is an insurance premium?
choices: The price paid to maintain insurance coverage
The maximum possible payment for every claim
A loan made to the policyholder
A penalty paid only after an accident

questions.question: What is a deductible in a typical property insurance policy?
choices: The insurer's yearly advertising expense
The amount borrowed to buy the property
The value of every item in a house
The portion of a covered loss paid by the policyholder

questions.question: What is an insurance claim?
choices: A request to open a checking account
A request for payment or benefits under a policy
A loan application based on the policy's price
A guarantee that a policy will cover every loss

questions.question: What is a coverage limit?
choices: The maximum a policy pays for a specified covered loss or category
The minimum income required to own property
The number of companies allowed to sell insurance
The amount every customer must save monthly

questions.question: What is a policy exclusion?
choices: A benefit automatically paid without a loss
A refund of the entire annual premium
A condition or type of loss the policy does not cover
A discount required on every renewal

questions.question: What does liability insurance generally address?
choices: Normal declines in an investment's market price
Every routine maintenance cost of a home
The cost of purchases made on credit
Covered claims for injury or damage for which the insured is responsible

questions.question: How does risk pooling help insurance work?
choices: Each person pays only after experiencing a loss
Payments from many policyholders help fund covered losses suffered by some
Every policyholder must suffer an identical loss
The insurer promises that losses will never occur

questions.question: Why might a higher deductible be associated with a lower premium?
choices: The policyholder takes responsibility for more of a covered loss
The insurer agrees to cover every excluded event
The policyholder stops being responsible for any loss
The policy's coverage limit automatically becomes unlimited

questions.question: Why is the lowest premium not always the best basis for comparing policies?
choices: Premiums never affect household costs
Every policy has identical coverage
Coverage, deductibles, limits, and exclusions can differ
Higher premiums guarantee no claims will be denied

questions.question: What is the main purpose of life insurance?
choices: To cover routine vehicle repairs
To guarantee a stock portfolio's return
To pay every medical bill without conditions
To provide specified benefits to beneficiaries after an insured person's death

questions.question: What distinguishes disability insurance from ordinary property insurance?
choices: It replaces a damaged roof after a storm
It can replace part of income when a covered disability prevents work
It protects only the value of household furniture
It guarantees repayment of every investment loss

questions.question: Why is renters insurance different from a landlord's building insurance?
choices: It can protect a renter's belongings and personal liability
It automatically gives the renter ownership of the building
It pays the landlord's property taxes directly
It guarantees that rent will never increase

questions.question: Why should a person read the policy rather than assume all damage is covered?
choices: Insurance contracts contain no coverage rules
Every policy covers the same events regardless of wording
The contract defines which losses and conditions are covered
A premium receipt replaces every term of the policy

questions.question: How can an inventory of household belongings help after a covered loss?
choices: It guarantees payment above the policy limit
It eliminates the deductible automatically
It changes excluded losses into covered losses
It helps document what was owned and its value

questions.question: A covered property loss is $2,000 with a $500 deductible. Assume no other limits or adjustments. How much does the insurer pay?
Policy A has a $250 deductible; Policy B has a $1,000 deductible. For the same covered loss above both amounts, which requires more initial cost-sharing?
choices: Policy B
Policy A
Both require exactly $250
Neither requires cost-sharing

questions.question: A family lives where flooding is possible. What should it check before relying on a standard homeowners policy?
choices: Whether premiums are paid monthly or annually
Whether the policy covers theft of personal belongings
Whether flood damage is covered or needs separate coverage
Whether the insurer offers a discount for installing smoke alarms

questions.question: A policy costs $40 per month. With no price change, what is the total annual premium?
A driver injures another person in a crash for which the driver is legally responsible. Which coverage is most directly relevant?
choices: Life insurance on the driver
Auto bodily injury liability coverage
Home contents coverage
Disability coverage for an unrelated worker
